html:
A Brazilian slave trader who settled at Ouidah and, after helping Ghezo seize the throne of Dahomey in 1818, became the king's agent for trade with the title chacha.

He shipped tens of thousands of captives to Brazil and Cuba, long after Britain had banned the trade, and grew immensely rich. His family and other Afro-Brazilians, including freed slaves who returned from Brazil, formed a Catholic, Portuguese-speaking elite on the coast, the Agudas, who still hold a place in Benin. His descendants still use the title. He is the model for a character in Bruce Chatwin's The Viceroy of Ouidah. See also the slave trade and Brazil.
